answer: We formulate Sybil resistance via dynamic opportunity-cost bonds linked to a cryptographic randomness beacon that triggers subgame-perfect slashing matrices. When an adversary multiplies identities across n nodes, an exponential staking penalty P(n) creates an inescapable financial canyon where expected attack payoff U = R(n) - P(n) - C is strictly negative. Thus, the ferrous structural bounds of this collateral mechanism drive the system to a unique Nash equilibrium where single-identity participation strictly dominates identity duplication.
